c.request: Link each invoice line item to its product (by product id) and to that product's category (by production type code), dropping lines with no match. For each product type description, compute the average `product_quantity` and the average difference between `derived_product_cost` and `derived_total_cost` per line (ignore missing values). Then keep only the categories whose average difference is above the mean of all the category averages. Return one row with three values: the average of those categories' average quantity, the average of their average difference, and the average of how much their average difference exceeds that mean. Don't round anything. The per-line difference is product cost minus total cost, keeping its sign.
c.sql: WITH line_items_with_categories AS (SELECT ili.order_item_id, ili.invoice_number, ili.product_id, ili.product_quantity, ili.derived_product_cost, ili.derived_total_cost, p.production_type_code, pc.product_type_description, (ili.derived_product_cost - ili.derived_total_cost) AS cost_difference FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili INNER JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id INNER JOIN Product_Categories pc ON p.production_type_code = pc.production_type_code), category_averages AS (SELECT product_type_description, AVG(CASE WHEN product_quantity IS NOT NULL THEN CAST(product_quantity AS DECIMAL(19,4)) END) AS avg_quantity, AVG(CASE WHEN derived_product_cost IS NOT NULL AND derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL THEN (derived_product_cost - derived_total_cost) END) AS avg_difference FROM line_items_with_categories GROUP BY product_type_description), mean_of_averages AS (SELECT AVG(avg_difference) AS overall_mean_difference FROM category_averages), filtered_categories AS (SELECT ca.product_type_description, ca.avg_quantity, ca.avg_difference, ca.avg_difference - moa.overall_mean_difference AS difference_above_mean FROM category_averages ca CROSS JOIN mean_of_averages moa WHERE ca.avg_difference > moa.overall_mean_difference) SELECT AVG(avg_quantity) AS avg_of_avg_quantities, AVG(avg_difference) AS avg_of_avg_differences, AVG(difference_above_mean) AS avg_of_differences_above_mean FROM filtered_categories

b.request: Join Invoice_Line_Items to Products to Product_Categories (inner joins), compute per-category average product_quantity and average (derived_product_cost - derived_total_cost), retain only categories whose average difference exceeds the mean of all category average differences, return one row with: the average of those retained categories' average quantities, the average of their average differences, and the average amount by which their average differences exceed the overall mean.
b.sql: WITH category_stats AS (SELECT pc.production_type_code, AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS DECIMAL(19,4))) as avg_quantity, AVG(ili.derived_product_cost - ili.derived_total_cost) as avg_difference FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili INNER JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id INNER JOIN Product_Categories pc ON p.production_type_code = pc.production_type_code GROUP BY pc.production_type_code), overall_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_difference) as mean_difference FROM category_stats), retained_categories AS (SELECT cs.avg_quantity, cs.avg_difference, om.mean_difference FROM category_stats cs CROSS JOIN overall_mean om WHERE cs.avg_difference > om.mean_difference) SELECT AVG(avg_quantity) as avg_of_avg_quantities, AVG(avg_difference) as avg_of_avg_differences, AVG(avg_difference - mean_difference) as avg_excess_above_mean FROM retained_categories

a.request: Link each invoice line item to its product (by product id) and to that product's category (by production type code), dropping lines with no match. For each product type description, compute the average `product_quantity` and the average cost difference, where each line's cost difference is `derived_product_cost` minus `derived_total_cost` (ignore missing values). Then take the mean of those category averages and keep only the categories whose average cost difference is above that mean. Return one row with three values: the average of those categories' average quantity, the average of their average cost difference, and the average of how much their average cost difference exceeds the mean. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH category_averages AS (SELECT pc.product_type_description, AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS DECIMAL(19,4))) as avg_quantity, AVG(ili.derived_product_cost - ili.derived_total_cost) as avg_cost_difference FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili INNER JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id INNER JOIN Product_Categories pc ON p.production_type_code = pc.production_type_code GROUP BY pc.product_type_description), mean_cost_difference AS (SELECT AVG(avg_cost_difference) as mean_avg_cost_diff FROM category_averages), filtered_categories AS (SELECT ca.avg_quantity, ca.avg_cost_difference, mcd.mean_avg_cost_diff FROM category_averages ca CROSS JOIN mean_cost_difference mcd WHERE ca.avg_cost_difference > mcd.mean_avg_cost_diff) SELECT AVG(avg_quantity) as avg_of_avg_quantities, AVG(avg_cost_difference) as avg_of_avg_cost_differences, AVG(avg_cost_difference - mean_avg_cost_diff) as avg_exceeds_mean FROM filtered_categories

d.request: For each product category, compute the average product_quantity and average (derived_product_cost - derived_total_cost) per line item, then filter to categories whose average difference exceeds the mean of all category average differences, and return the average of the filtered categories' average quantities, the average of their average differences, and the average amount by which their average differences exceed the overall mean.
d.sql: WITH category_stats AS (SELECT pc.production_type_code, AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS DECIMAL(19,4))) as avg_quantity, AVG(ili.derived_product_cost - ili.derived_total_cost) as avg_difference FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id JOIN Product_Categories pc ON p.production_type_code = pc.production_type_code GROUP BY pc.production_type_code), overall_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_difference) as mean_difference FROM category_stats), filtered_categories AS (SELECT cs.avg_quantity, cs.avg_difference, om.mean_difference FROM category_stats cs CROSS JOIN overall_mean om WHERE cs.avg_difference > om.mean_difference) SELECT AVG(avg_quantity) as avg_of_avg_quantities, AVG(avg_difference) as avg_of_avg_differences, AVG(avg_difference - mean_difference) as avg_excess_over_mean FROM filtered_categories
